query: For high-entropy alloys used in thermal-insulation applications, what testable hypothesis could be made about an unspecified predictive approach for accurately identifying materials with low phonon thermal conductivity? The hypothesis should explain why the approach would work, predict its improvement over current predictions, define its applicability limits, identify supporting evidence, and specify a decisive experimental benchmark and outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: A DFT-ML predictive model that integrates force-constant fluctuation descriptors—which are calibrated using both binary alloy calculations and a curated set of multi-component HEA data—can identify single-phase HEA compositions that exhibit quantifiable lattice distortions exceeding 20% and achieve predicted phonon thermal conductivity values at least 30% lower than those from conventional DFT methods.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase, equiatomic high-entropy alloys (e.g., FeCoCrMnNi) synthesized as solid solutions.
generation.intervention: Implement a combined DFT and machine learning framework that calculates force-constant fluctuation descriptors and lattice distortion metrics from both binary systems and selected multi-component HEA data, using defined protocols (e.g., XRD line broadening and TEM diffraction analysis) to quantify >20% lattice distortivity.
generation.conditions: Predictions are made at room temperature and moderately elevated temperatures (300–500 K) under equilibrium conditions.
generation.structural_mediator: Measured lattice distortions and force-constant fluctuations; experimentally verified by diffraction techniques showing >20% variation in interatomic force constants.
generation.mechanism: High configurational entropy in multi-principal element alloys induces severe lattice distortions that enhance phonon scattering and reduce phonon mean free paths, thereby lowering the lattice thermal conductivity.
generation.predicted_outcome: The model predicts HEAs with calculated lattice thermal conductivity values at least 30% lower than those predicted by standard DFT-only approaches, with an overall prediction accuracy improved by roughly 20% over baseline methods.
generation.baseline: Conventional first-principles predictions that do not incorporate transferable descriptors from binary or limited multi-component data.
generation.boundary: Applicable to HEAs whose compositions and bonding environments are similar to those in the curated training datasets, typically systems containing 4–7 principal elements.
generation.uncertainty: While the incorporation of multi-component training data mitigates transferability concerns, uncertainty remains in how universally the binary-derived descriptors apply; however, early experimental correlations (e.g., from diffraction studies) support the basic premise.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize a series of predicted low thermal conductivity HEAs and measure their lattice thermal conductivity via transient laser flash analysis. Verify the extent of lattice distortion using diffraction (XRD, TEM) and inelastic neutron scattering to assess phonon linewidths.
measurements: Lattice thermal conductivity values from experimental laser flash or transient plane source methods.
XRD and TEM measurements to confirm lattice distortion (>20% force-constant fluctuations).
Inelastic neutron scattering to quantify phonon linewidth broadening.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the experimentally measured lattice thermal conductivity is not at least 30% lower than those predicted by conventional DFT methods, or if the expected lattice distortions (>20%) are not observed, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: It is clearly observed that the (4RE0.25)2(Zr0.75Ce0.25)2O7 porous high-entropy ceramics presented lower thermal conductivity values, which demonstrates their potential application as thermal insulation materials. Optical and infrared images are shown in Figure 11. The thickness of the testing sample is 7.08 mm. Figure 11a clearly exhibits the experimental process. The temperature of the flame can reach 1204 °C, which is presented in Figure 11b. With the alumina fiber block, the flame can be concentrated and stabilized. As shown in Figure 11c–f, the temperature of the back can reach 340.4 °C during the long testing process (1 h) before the sample has obvious cracks. This also indicates that the sample could withstand prolonged high-temperature flames. Therefore, the (4RE0.25)2(Zr0.75Ce0.25)2O7 porous high-entropy ceramics have good thermal stability and insulation performance.

In conclusion, we have reported the first experimental investigation of the acoustic phonon dispersions in a High-Entropy Alloy, complemented by the GVDOS survey, at room and low temperature. FeCoCrMnNi is a 5-element random alloy, and, despite the inherent disorder, its phonon dynamics closely resemble that of the pure elements composing it and the corresponding binary alloys. More specifically, acoustic phonons disperse throughout the whole Brillouin zone up to energies between 20 and 30 meV, exhibiting an attenuation stronger than in simple elements, but of the same order of magnitude as in binary alloys. The whole attenuation behavior can be understood in terms of scattering from force-constant fluctuations, which have been estimated to amount to ~20% using a simple theoretical model, a value comparable with calculations of Mu and co-authors on binary and ternary alloys made of the same elements. If this is unexpected from Mu’s theory, which would predict increased force-constant fluctuations due to the larger variability of random environments of a given atomic pair, it explains recent experimental reports on comparable phonon lattice thermal conductivities in our HEA and FeNi

Recently, PbSnTeSe has been experimentally investigated by Fan et al. [] and Raphel et al. [,], who report appreciably similar results for the thermoelectric performance of the material (see below). The modelling of HEAs transport properties constitute a challenge, and both the simulation methods and their derived predictions have to be confronted to experimental data to assess their validity. In this context, we present in this paper for the first time a complete approach that allows one to obtain all the transport coefficients, including the figure of merit, of a high-entropy alloy. The thermoelectric transport properties of the PbSnTeSe high-entropy alloy have been calculated by combining state-of-the-art methods based on the special quasi-random structures approach to generate the HEA structure, the first-principles density-functional theory (DFT), and the Boltzmann transport and Green–Kubo theories. First, from the DFT-computed material electronic states, the electronic transport properties (electronic conductivity, Seebeck coefficient and electronic thermal conductivity) were calculated using the linearized Boltzmann transport equation, and the power factor was obtained. papers.title: Rare-Earth-Zirconate Porous High-Entropy Ceramics with Unique Pore Structures for Thermal Insulating Applications.
papers.system: Rare-earth zirconate based high-entropy ceramics with tailored porous structures
papers.approach: Experimental fabrication via a TBA-based gel-casting method with controlled solid loadings, followed by thermal and mechanical characterization
papers.findings: The ceramics exhibit ultra-low thermal conductivity (e.g., 0.0642–0.1213 W/(m·K) at room temperature) and good thermal stability under high-temperature flame conditions, attributed to both high-entropy induced lattice distortions and the unique pore architecture that scatters phonons.
papers.mechanism: Lattice distortion from multi-refractory species increases phonon scattering; the controlled, uniform micro-porosity further interrupts phonon transport.

papers.title: Phonon behavior in a random solid solution: a lattice dynamics study on the high-entropy alloy FeCoCrMnNi.
papers.approach: Combined inelastic neutron and X-ray scattering experiments alongside lattice dynamics simulations
papers.findings: Acoustic phonon dispersions show strong attenuation due to disorder; force-constant fluctuations (estimated between 20–50%) lead to significant phonon scattering. Despite the expected increase with more elements, the scattering levels compare with those observed in binary or ternary alloys.
papers.mechanism: Scattering mainly arises from force-constant fluctuations induced by chemical disorder, yet the increase in constituent elements does not linearly boost phonon attenuation as theory might suggest.

papers.title: Dual-Porosity (Ta0.2Nb0.2Ti0.2Zr0.2Hf0.2)C High-Entropy Ceramics with High Compressive Strength
papers.system: Carbide high-entropy ceramics (Ta0.2Nb0.2Ti0.2Zr0.2Hf0.2)C with engineered dual-porosity
papers.approach: Pressureless sintering using a mixture of ceramic precursor and pore-formers (SiO2 microspheres), with subsequent characterization of thermal conductivity and compressive strength
papers.findings: The dual-porosity design leads to very low intrinsic thermal conductivity (as low as ~0.5 W·m−1·K−1 in some samples) while maintaining excellent mechanical strength, compared to both conventional ultra-high temperature ceramics and single-pore counterparts.
papers.mechanism: Severe lattice distortions from multi-element effects shorten phonon mean free paths; in addition, dual pore sizes enhance scattering, curtailing heat conduction and simultaneously deflecting crack propagation.

papers.title: Investigation of PbSnTeSe High-Entropy Thermoelectric Alloy: A DFT Approach.
papers.system: PbSnTeSe high-entropy alloy for thermoelectric applications
papers.approach: First-principles density-functional theory (DFT) combined with on-the-fly machine-learned force fields and Green–Kubo simulations to compute transport coefficients
papers.findings: The calculated lattice thermal conductivity is very low (<0.4 W/(m·K)) at room temperature, supporting the notion that high entropy and associated lattice distortions significantly suppress phonon heat conduction in these alloys.
papers.mechanism: The intrinsic lattice distortions due to multiple principal elements reduce phonon velocity and enhance scattering, resulting in diminished lattice thermal conductivity.

papers.title: Ab initio study of mechanical and thermal properties of GeTe-based and PbSe-based high-entropy chalcogenides.
papers.approach: Ab initio DFT calculations to evaluate elastic and thermal transport properties, including analyses of Debye temperatures, Grüneisen parameters, and phonon dispersion trends
papers.findings: Alloying elements (e.g., Pb, Bi) in these systems increase mass and strain-field fluctuations that enhance phonon scattering. The strengthened anharmonicity and reduced sound velocity correlate with lower lattice thermal conductivity.
papers.mechanism: Enhanced bond anharmonicity and internal elastic strain fields cause reduced phonon velocities and increased phonon-phonon interactions, thus limiting heat conduction.

papers.title: Exploring thermophysical properties of CoCrFeNiCu high entropy alloy via molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.approach: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to examine lattice thermal conductivity, volumetric specific heat, and phonon density of states as functions of temperature, composition, and system size
papers.findings: Lattice thermal conductivity (kp) increases with simulation domain size and is sensitive to chemical composition and temperature. The inherent disorder and lattice distortion from differing atomic sizes result in enhanced phonon scattering and reduced kp.
papers.mechanism: Chemical disorder induces lattice distortions which shorten the phonon mean free path; also, finite size effects in simulation indicate that phonon transport is strongly dependent on the scattering length scales set by the atomic configuration.

papers.title: High-throughput materials screening algorithm based on first-principles density functional theory and artificial neural network for high-entropy alloy
papers.approach: A combined KKR-CPA method with machine learning to rapidly screen the vast configurational space of HEAs based on first-principles calculations
papers.findings: The integrated approach successfully predicts properties (including formation energies and structural information) for HEAs while significantly reducing computational cost relative to brute-force DFT calculations.
papers.mechanism: Machine learning leverages trends from simpler systems (binaries) to extrapolate to multi-component HEAs, effectively capturing the role of disorder and configurational entropy.

papers.title: Entropy engineering promotes thermoelectric performance in p-type chalcogenides.
papers.approach: Experimental demonstration of entropy engineering strategies to optimize both electrical and thermal transport properties in thermoelectric materials
papers.findings: Increased elemental diversity leads to severe lattice distortions that scatter heat-carrying phonons effectively, resulting in reduced lattice thermal conductivity and improved thermoelectric performance.
papers.mechanism: High configurational entropy stabilizes single-phase structures and induces atomic-level distortions that intensify phonon scattering while reducing adverse phase-boundary effects.

papers.title: Accelerated crystal structure prediction of multi-elements random alloy using expandable features.
papers.approach: A machine learning-based crystal structure prediction approach that transforms raw features into an expandable form, trained on binary alloy data to predict HEA phases
papers.findings: Without explicit HEA training data, the method achieves accuracies of over 80% in predicting the crystal structures of HEAs, promising a massive reduction in computational cost.
papers.mechanism: The transformation module facilitates feature expansion so that trends learned from binary systems can be transferred to complex multi-element alloys.

directions.direction: Develop an integrated DFT‐ML predictive model that uses force‐constant fluctuations and lattice distortion descriptors extracted from binary systems to forecast the low lattice thermal conductivity of HEAs.
directions.assessment: This approach directly targets the phonon scattering mechanism in HEAs by quantifying lattice distortions. It leverages established DFT evidence (e.g., force‐constant fluctuations of 20–50% in FeCoCrMnNi, see PMC9726824::web::014) and previous success in screening HEAs (PMC9534987::web::005). The physics of strong lattice distortions causing low phonon conductivity is well supported. Data transfer from binary to multi‐component systems is challenging but promising.

directions.direction: Apply mesoscale molecular dynamics simulations that explicitly account for finite-size effects to predict phonon transport in HEAs.
directions.assessment: Incorporating size effects (as shown in PMC11369437::web::018 and PMC11369437::web::014) directly relates to phonon mean free path issues in HEAs. This approach improves current simulation predictions by mitigating domain-size artifacts. The underlying simulation physics is well established but demands careful validation.

directions.direction: Use a high-throughput screening algorithm with expandable feature embedding trained on binary alloy datasets to predict the low phonon thermal conductivity phase space for HEAs.
directions.type: modeling/machine learning and high-throughput materials screening
directions.assessment: Based on the evidence of successful phase prediction in multi-element alloys from binary data (PMC7933338::web::000), this approach would relieve the computational cost barrier. It directly attacks the problem by extending known chemical trends into HEAs, although its applicability may be limited by the training set's representativity.

directions.direction: Integrate in situ phonon scattering measurements using inelastic neutron/X-ray scattering with the predictive framework to calibrate and validate model predictions.
directions.type: characterization/mechanism study with data-driven model calibration
directions.assessment: This hybrid approach uses direct phonon linewidth and dispersion data (as in PMC9726824::web::010 and PMC9726824::web::014) to constrain and refine predictions. It directly measures the scattering mechanisms that lower thermal conductivity. Although experimental complexity is higher, it offers a decisive benchmark linking simulations and measurements.

directions.direction: Establish a dual-porosity HEA experimental synthesis route combined with predictive thermal modeling to study how engineered microstructure (e.g., controlled porosity) enhances phonon scattering.
directions.type: composition design and processing synthesis coupled with modeling
directions.assessment: Drawing on examples from porous high-entropy ceramics (PMC10143762::web::023 and PMC10052925::web::018), this direction explores synergy between chemical disorder and engineered porosity. It addresses thickness and interface effects on thermal transport. The physics is well-supported but might be constrained to ceramic-based systems rather than metallic HEAs.
